title: Greenslate rollout playpad and release notes (May 2027) - draft
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight, low-risk rollout playpad for the Greenslate feature pack (models + routing + small infra change). Goal is a quiet-window, incrementally ramped rollout with clear hold gates and a concise release-notes draft for customer-facing channels.

Scope and constraints:
- Non-breaking: no DB schema changes.
- Target audience: hosted API customers and internal Dedicated pools.
- Rollout window: local timezone-friendly quiet hours (US-PST overnight) to minimize customer impact.
- Safety: fast rollback path + telemetry SLO gates.

High-level timeline (calendar):
- Day -7 (2027-05-03): Branch freeze for Greenslate, final smoke test matrix updated. Owners: Maya (release), Ravi (tests).
- Day -3 (2027-05-07): Canary build deployed to staging and internal beta. Quick load test (5k reqs) and perf bench (p95 latency). Owners: Liam (infra), Elena (perf).
- Day -1 (2027-05-09): Preflight checklist completed; release notes draft reviewed by docs.
- Launch day (2027-05-10): 02:00 PST start, progressive traffic ramp for 6 hours.
- Day +1 (2027-05-11): Hold window for 24h monitoring, prepare patch if needed.
- Day +7 (2027-05-17): Post-rollout retro + final release notes and changelog update.

Progressive ramp plan (launch day detailed):
- 02:00 PST: baseline snapshot + deploy to routing layer (no traffic). Run quick smoke (2m).
- 02:10 PST: enable 1% traffic to Greenslate variants, 30m hold. Telemetry: latency p95, error rate, token cost delta.
- 02:40 PST: if metrics stable, 5% traffic, 60m hold.
- 03:40 PST: 20% traffic, 90m hold.
- 05:10 PST: 50% traffic, 120m hold.
- 07:10 PST: 100% traffic (finish ramp) if all gates passed.
Notes: each hold requires explicit sign-off in #release-ops channel by on-call + release lead. Failure to sign off -> automatic rollback to previous routing config.

Preflight checklist (quick tasks, tick when complete):
- [ ] Code merge: green CI, security scan passed (Snyk/GH actions).
- [ ] Smoke test suite (critical user journeys) passing on staging.
- [ ] Load test baseline (p95 latency delta < +10% vs baseline).
- [ ] Dependency matrix validated (quantization changes verified on serving instances).
- [ ] Capacity reservations made for Dedicated pools (if using reserved capacity).
- [ ] KMS key policy reviewed for private deployments (Elena).
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards deployed and bookmarked (latency p50/p95, error-rate, rate-limit hits, token-unit cost).
- [ ] Alert thresholds configured (see alert table below).
- [ ] Runbook updated and on-call assigned for launch night.

Alert thresholds (initial):
- Error rate (5xx or application errors) > 0.5% over baseline for 5m -> investigate, hold ramp.
- p95 latency > baseline + 25% for 10m -> hold ramp + paging.
- Token cost per request increase > 30% -> hold ramp + notify product.
- Rate limit spike (customer returned 429s) -> route to safety lane (fallback model), hold ramp.

Rollback matrix (quick reference):
- Symptom: sudden spike in 5xx across all regions -> Action: immediate rollback to previous routing variant, page SRE, open hotpatch PR.
- Symptom: sustained p95 degradation > 40% -> Action: pause ramp, reduce to previous stable split (e.g., back to 5%), run targeted perf reproduction, escalate to perf owner.
- Symptom: cost spike on tokens with no visible perf improvement -> Action: pause rollout, revert model quantization profile, notify product to triage NLU quality.
- Symptom: single-customer regression (error or integrity issue) -> Action: isolate using customer routing rules, initiate patch for specific customer if possible, otherwise hold/rollback.

Communication templates (for quick copy):
- Slack short: "Greenslate ramp: currently at {N}% as of {time}. Monitoring p95/error/cost. No blockers so far. Ping @release-ops for sign-off to proceed."
- Outbound customer note (if visible regression): "We've temporarily reduced exposure to the Greenslate models for traffic safety while we investigate a performance regression affecting some requests. We'll post updates in the status page and follow up with SLA impact if any."

Release notes draft (customer-facing, brief):
Title: Greenslate feature pack (May 2027)
Summary: Small, incremental rollout of model routing improvements and new Greenslate model variants. Objective: reduce hallucination in short-form completions and reduce tokenization overhead for common prompt patterns.
What changed:
- Added Greenslate-1 and Greenslate-1-quant model variants to hosted catalog (non-breaking).
- Updated smart-routing policy: requests with short-form prompts are preferentially routed to Greenslate-1 when eligible.
- Minor runtime optimization: improved KV cache reuse in multi-turn sessions (expected token-cost reduction ~10% on average).
Migration notes:
- No action required from customers. Clients using pinned model names will not be affected.
Known issues (initial):
- A small subset of prompt templates may see slightly different tokenization behavior; if you rely on exact token counts for downstream billing, contact support.
- Internal: we have an open investigation on p95 jitter for sessions > 2k tokens (low likelihood for most users).
We’ll update this page after the 24h monitoring window.

Post-release checklist (Day +1 and Day +7):
- Day +1: confirm telemetry stable for 24h at 100% traffic, finalize release notes and mark doc status -> final.
- Day +3: collect a sampling of user queries for qualitative evals (product + applied-ml).
- Day +7: retro: list what went well, what didn't, and action items tracked in ENG-10234.

Owners and roles (who does what):
- Release lead: Maya Patel (coordination, go/no-go).
- Infra & deployment: Liam O'Connor (routing, autoscale knobs).
- Perf & telemetry: Elena Gomez (dashboards, thresholds).
- QA & smoke: Ravi Singh (preflight, test triage).
- Docs & comms: Ashley Kim (customer-facing release notes and changelog).
- SRE on-call: (rotation) refer to runbook.

Open questions / loose ends (notes to self):
- Confirm whether Dedicated pools require a separate gating policy (Ravi to confirm by Day -2).
- Ensure quantized variant benchmarks include memory consumption snapshot for small GPU classes.
- Decide whether to include the Greenslate training eval artifact link in customer notes (privacy considerations).

Quick links for on-call:
- Perf dashboard: (bookmark) /d/perf/greenslate-launch
- Error alerts: /alerts/greenslate-error
- Rollback toggle: /ops/routing/rollbacks/greenslate

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep the ramp conservative; the whole point of Greenslate is marginal unit-economics improvement without customer disruption. If in doubt, hold.
- If we observe a silent quality regression captured by evals, do not proceed to 100% until product signs off.

Appendix: small checklist for postmortem capture (if incident occurs):
- Timeline minute-by-minute from deploy start.
- Snapshots of p95/p99, error counts, token cost delta at each ramp step.
- A/B comparison sample of 30 requests pre/post showing quality delta.
- Action item owner and deadline for each remediation.

End of draft.

----
Revision history:
- 2027-05-10: initial draft (Maya)
- 2027-05-11: telemetry thresholds tuned, added rollback matrix (Elena)
- 2027-05-12: release notes copy edits and links added (Ashley)
